subtitle: Lists UCLA Campus Computing Network contacts for ARPANET users.

tldr.problem: ARPANET users needed to know which UCLA CCN contact handled administrative, technical, programming and operations issues.
tldr.mechanism: The memo lists six contacts and explains which roles users should approach for specific concerns.

today: RFC 423 updates RFC 389. It is a historical contact list with names and telephone numbers from December 1972.

sections.title: The UCLA CCN Contact List
sections.content:
Barbara B. Noble of UCLA-CCN sent this notice to ARPA Network users on December 12, 1972. The contact list covers initial contact, ARPA liaison, network technical liaison, operations manager, operations and consulting.

The unit metadata records that RFC 423 updates RFC 389.
sections.plainLanguage: The notice names contacts at UCLA CCN and describes their areas of responsibility. It updates an earlier contact list.

sections.title: Administrative and Technical Matters
sections.content:
For administrative matters and general facility orientation, users are directed to Bob Bell, Head of User Relations. He or Doug Cummings handles matters such as charge number applications and funding and can discuss CCN facilities and services.

For network technical matters, Robert Braden, Manager of Programming, handles problems with Network protocol and hardware.
sections.plainLanguage: New users contact User Relations about facility access and administration. Network protocol or hardware problems go to the technical liaison.

sections.title: Support While Using CCN
sections.content:
For programming problems such as JCL, compilers and documentation, and other issues related to using CCN, Barbara Noble is the focal point. The notice says she will try to solve programming problems and expedite other matters.

Questions about schedules and special handling go to Operations or the Operations Manager.
sections.plainLanguage: Barbara Noble is the main contact for programming and user problems. Operations questions go to the operations staff.
